MUSIC AND DANCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: MUSIC AND DANCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Remove the need for rules
   B. Replace drinking water
   C. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
   D. Guarantee a trophy

2. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Brown, pink, and gold
   B. Black, white, and grey
   C. Red, blue, and yellow
   D. Green, orange, and purple

3. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   D. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

4. Best practice when working on Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instruments 2.4 Western Musical Instruments 2.5 Contem: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instruments 2.4 Western Musical Instruments 2.5 Contem with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instruments 2.4 Western Musical Instruments 2.5 Contem.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instruments 2.4 Western Musical Instruments 2.5 Contem.
   D. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instruments 2.4 Western Musical Instruments 2.5 Contem.

5. Best practice when working on Two-Part Harmony Two-part harmony guidelines;: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Two-Part Harmony Two-part harmony guidelines; with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Two-Part Harmony Two-part harmony guidelines;.
   C. Damage equipment used for Two-Part Harmony Two-part harmony guidelines;.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Two-Part Harmony Two-part harmony guidelines;.

6. Best practice when working on Kenyan Folk Songs: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Kenyan Folk Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Folk Songs.
   C. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Folk Songs.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Folk Songs.

7. Best practice when working on Music Notation Software 1.7 Dance Production 2.0 Performing 2.1 Kenyan Folk Song: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Music Notation Software 1.7 Dance Production 2.0 Performing 2.1 Kenyan Folk Song.
   B. Damage equipment used for Music Notation Software 1.7 Dance Production 2.0 Performing 2.1 Kenyan Folk Song.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Music Notation Software 1.7 Dance Production 2.0 Performing 2.1 Kenyan Folk Song.
   D. Practise Music Notation Software 1.7 Dance Production 2.0 Performing 2.1 Kenyan Folk Song with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

8. Best practice when working on Dance Production: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Dance Production.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Dance Production.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Dance Production.

9. Best practice when working on Kenyan Folk Songs 2.2 Western Style Solo Songs 2.3 Kenyan Indigenous Musical Ins: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Kenyan Folk Songs 2.2 Western Style Solo Songs 2.3 Kenyan Indigenous Musical Ins with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

   C. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Folk Songs 2.2 Western Style Solo Songs 2.3 Kenyan Indigenous Musical Ins.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Folk Songs 2.2 Western Style Solo Songs 2.3 Kenyan Indigenous Musical Ins.

10. Best practice when working on Melody in Major Keys: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Melody in Major Keys.
   B. Practise Melody in Major Keys with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Melody in Major Keys.

11. Best practice when working on Western Style Solo Songs: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Western Style Solo Songs.

   C. Refuse all feedback on Western Style Solo Songs.

12. Best practice when working on Music Notation Software: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Music Notation Software.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Kenyan Folk Songs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Classical Music and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Music and Dance in Socio-Cultural Context Page 15 of 59 1 STRAND 1.0: FOUNDATION and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Music and Dance in Socio-cultural Context and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

4. A — Practise Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instruments 2.4 Western Musical Instruments 2.5 Contem with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. A — Practise Kenyan Folk Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. D — Practise Music Notation Software 1.7 Dance Production 2.0 Performing 2.1 Kenyan Folk Song with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

8. A — Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

9. A — Practise Kenyan Folk Songs 2.2 Western Style Solo Songs 2.3 Kenyan Indigenous Musical Ins with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. D — Practise Western Style Solo Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. C — Practise Music Notation Software with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Kenyan Folk Songs; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Music and Dance in Socio-cultural Context; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
